claims.text: The frozen source variants ask for a 500k-QPS/OPS in-app unread-message system and preserve unread-message, recipient/inverted-index, sharded-storage, high-concurrency and Redis concerns; they do not provide a production traffic mix, node count, message size, retention, SLO or measured per-shard throughput.

The candidate treats 500k as a system workload target that must be split into query, ingest, fanout and read-state rates, and derives resource counts from measured safe per-shard throughput plus headroom rather than inventing universal Redis/Kafka node throughput.

The candidate keeps durable message/delivery/read-state facts separate from Redis materializations, uses Redis Cluster and sorted sets only as sharding/ordered-index primitives, and explicitly preserves Redis Cluster and WAIT write-safety/strong-consistency boundaries.

Fanout is defined as replayable and acknowledged only after a durable or idempotent side effect, with event_id plus recipient identity for deduplication, monotonic read cursor/version semantics, and reconciliation so duplicates, late events and rebuilds cannot permanently double-count or resurrect read messages.

The candidate separates targeted recipient fanout from high-fanout/system broadcasts, explains recipient-key sharding locality without claiming uniform hashing removes hot-user skew, and uses shared broadcast/topic state plus cursor/segment materialization as an alternative to synchronous O(all users) fanout.

The candidate requires latency/throughput, queue lag, pending/retry, Redis hit/skew, durable-store latency, unread drift and rebuild metrics, and requires target-environment 500k load, failover, hot-key and backlog-recovery tests before claiming the capacity target is proven.
